journal.text: First session, no prior journal or positions. Building an initial diversified core portfolio across mega-cap tech/quality names rather than concentrating in the most volatile momentum names (AVGO/NVDA/AMD/PLTR/CRWD have shown sharp swings and drawdowns over the past month, e.g. AVGO fell from ~403 to ~326 then partly recovered, PLTR down from ~198 to ~178). Chose MSFT, GOOGL, AMZN, AAPL, META as broad mega-cap tech exposure with reasonable recent stability; added LIN (industrial gas, low volatility) and COST (defensive consumer staple/retailer) for diversification away from pure tech; small AVGO and ADBE positions for semis/software exposure without overweighting the most volatile names. Kept ~$5k (10%) in cash as dry powder for opportunistic buys or to average down. Position sizes roughly $3.5k-$6k each, no single name dominates. Will reassess next session using price action: if any holding drops >8-10% without fundamental news I'll evaluate averaging down vs cutting; if broad market strength continues I may deploy remaining cash into laggards or add momentum names like NVDA on pullback confirmation.

Reviewed 10-day price history for core holdings plus NVDA/PLTR as momentum comparisons. Jan 2 saw a broad, market-wide pullback (MSFT -2.2%, GOOGL -0.6% but big intraday range, AMZN -1.9%, AAPL -0.3%, META -1.4%, ADBE -4.7%, AVGO -0.6%) with no single name showing an idiosyncratic drop that would suggest company-specific bad news - looks like general risk-off/rotation rather than a reason to cut positions. None of my holdings have hit the >8-10% single-name drawdown threshold from my initial plan that would trigger averaging down or cutting. Cash position is thin (~$5k, 10%) since last session's fills moved slightly against cost basis; keeping it as dry powder rather than chasing weakness on a single down day. Holding all positions unchanged today. Will reassess if the pullback persists or deepens into next session, or if any single name diverges meaningfully from the group (either sharp underperformance suggesting a cut, or a laggard like AVGO/ADBE showing a basing pattern worth adding to).

Reviewed 10-day history across holdings plus NVDA/PLTR. Jan 2 pullback (broad, market-wide) partially reversed on Jan 5 for most names: GOOGL, AMZN, META, LIN, COST, AVGO all bounced back toward or above pre-selloff levels. AAPL and ADBE remain relative laggards (AAPL down to ~267, near recent lows; ADBE flat near 331-333, well off its ~350-357 range from mid-Dec) but neither has breached my >8-10% single-day/idiosyncratic-drop threshold that would trigger a trim - this still looks like sector rotation/multiple compression rather than company-specific bad news. No holding shows a divergence sharp enough to justify cutting, and no laggard has shown a clear basing/reversal pattern yet that would justify aggressive averaging down with the thin ~$5k cash cushion. Holding all positions unchanged again today; preserving cash as dry powder. Will reconsider if AAPL or ADBE continue lower without stabilizing (potential add on confirmed basing) or if any name gaps down >8-10% on clear bad news (potential trim).

Reviewed 10-day price action. Jan 6 session showed broad continued recovery from the Jan 2 pullback: AMZN +3.4%, COST +1.5%, LIN +0.9%, MSFT +1.2%, META +0.1%, AVGO flat, ADBE +1.3%. GOOGL roughly flat. AAPL is the one clear laggard, down another 1.8% to 262.36, now the 6th straight session without a bounce (from ~278 high Jan 2 to 262, about -6%). This is a persistent grind lower rather than a single-day idiosyncratic drop, but it hasn't yet crossed my 8-10% drawdown threshold, and there's no confirmed basing pattern to justify averaging down yet. Cash remains thin (~$5k) so I'm not chasing the bounce in the recovered names either - preserving optionality. Holding all positions unchanged again. Will reconsider AAPL specifically if it breaks below ~255 (approaching -10% from recent high) without stabilizing (trim candidate), or if it prints a clear reversal day with volume (add candidate). Will also look to deploy cash into further broad-market weakness if a real risk-off move develops rather than continued single-stock rotation.

Reviewed 15-day history. Broad recovery continues: MSFT +2.3% over 2 sessions to 483.47 (near recent highs), GOOGL +2.4% to 321.98, AMZN strong +3.5% to 241.56, COST +1.5% to 882.58 (near highs), LIN steady ~434, META flat ~649, AVGO flat ~343.5, ADBE +1.3% to 338.10. AAPL remains the lone laggard, down again to 260.33 (-6.3% from Jan 2 high of 277.84, -9.4% from Dec 19 high of 278.84) - a persistent grind but not a sharp single-day drop, and no clear basing/reversal signal yet to justify adding. It's approaching but hasn't cleanly breached the 8-10% idiosyncratic-drawdown threshold from my plan. With cash still thin (~$5k, 10%) and no confirmed reversal, continuing to hold rather than trim into weakness or chase the broad bounce. Will reconsider AAPL if it breaks decisively below ~250 (>10% from recent high, trim candidate) or prints a strong reversal/volume day (add candidate).

Reviewed 20-day history. Broad names continue firming: GOOGL +2.5% to 325.44 (new local high), COST surged to 915.31 (+3.7% day, breaking to new highs), AMZN +2% to 246.29 continuing its recovery, LIN +1.3% to 439.69 near highs, ADBE flat/steady ~339, META modest bounce to 646.06, MSFT pulled back slightly to 478.11 after a strong run, AVGO also pulled back to 332.48. AAPL ticked down again to 259.04 (-0.5% day), now about -6.8% from the Jan 2 high of 277.84 and -7.1% from the Dec 19 high - still a grinding decline, not a sharp single-day drop, and still short of my 8-10% idiosyncratic threshold. No confirmed reversal/basing signal yet. Cash remains thin (~$5k, ~10% of NAV) so not chasing the COST/GOOGL strength or averaging down AAPL without clearer signals. Holding all positions unchanged. Will reconsider AAPL if it breaks decisively below ~250 (trim candidate) or prints a strong reversal/volume day (add candidate); will consider trimming winners like COST if it looks extended/parabolic without further confirmation.

COST has run hard: +8.2% in the last 5 sessions (854.50 -> 924.88), including a gap-up parabolic day on Jan 8. Per my stated plan to trim extended winners without a clear pullback yet, trimming ~1.5 units (~$1,387 at last close) to lock in gains and rebuild cash buffer (thin at ~$5k / ~10% NAV). AAPL remains the laggard at 259.37, about -6.7% from the Jan 2 high of 277.84 - still a grinding decline, not a sharp drop, and hasn't cleared my 8-10% idiosyncratic threshold or shown a reversal/volume signal, so holding it unchanged rather than averaging down or trimming further. Other core positions (MSFT, GOOGL, AMZN, META, LIN, AVGO, ADBE) are firm/consolidating - no action. Will reconsider AAPL if it breaks decisively below ~250 (trim) or prints a strong reversal day (add). Will consider further COST trims if it keeps extending without consolidation, or redeploying the raised cash if AAPL or another name offers a clean entry.

COST continues to extend without consolidation: 943.08 close on Jan 12, up another ~2% from the 924.88 level noted in my prior trim (Jan 12) and now +10.3% over the last 6 sessions from the 854.50 low. Per my stated plan to keep trimming extended winners that don't pause, selling another 1.5 units (~$1,415 at last close) to continue rebuilding cash buffer, which was still thin at ~$6,380 (12.6% of NAV) before this trade. AAPL remains rangebound around 259-260, still about -6.7% from the Jan 2 high of 277.84 - no decisive break below 250 and no reversal signal, so continuing to hold rather than add or trim further. ADBE has pulled back to 327.65 (-3.4% from recent 339 level) but this is a mild pullback, not yet a clear idiosyncratic drawdown signal worth acting on. Other core positions (MSFT, GOOGL, AMZN, META, LIN, AVGO) are firm/consolidating in normal ranges - no action. Will reconsider AAPL if it breaks decisively below ~250 (trim) or prints a strong reversal day (add). Will continue trimming COST incrementally on further extension, or redeploy cash if AAPL/ADBE offer a clean basing entry.

ADBE broke down sharply on Jan 13: -5.4% single-day move to 309.93 on elevated volume (7.2M vs ~3M avg), taking it to a fresh multi-week low (intraday 307.91) and now -13.8% off the Dec 22 high of 357.53 and -8.6% off the Jan 8 local high of 339.04. This crosses my previously stated 8-10% idiosyncratic drawdown threshold with confirming volume, unlike the AAPL grind which has stayed rangebound without a decisive break. Trimming roughly half the ADBE position (5 of ~10 units, ~$1,550 at last close) to cut risk on the weakest/most acutely deteriorating name while keeping a reduced stake in case it stabilizes. Other positions: COST's advance has paused (941.93 vs 943.08 prior close, first flat/down day after the recent run) so holding rather than trimming further after two prior COST trims already rebuilt cash to ~15% of NAV. GOOGL continues making new highs (335.97) - no action, letting it run. AMZN, MSFT, META pulled back modestly (1-2%) within normal noise, not yet actionable. AAPL remains rangebound 259-261, no decisive break below 250 and no reversal signal - holding. LIN, AVGO steady - no action. Will reconsider re-adding ADBE if it shows a basing/reversal signal, or trim further if the breakdown accelerates (e.g., through 300 with continued volume). Will revisit AAPL threshold and COST extension as before.

Broad tech pullback on Jan 14 rather than idiosyncratic weakness: MSFT -2.4% to 459.38 (-8.7% off Dec 31 high), META -2.4% to 615.52 (-8.2% off recent high), AMZN -2.4% to 236.65 (-5.9% off Jan 9 high), AVGO -4.2% to 339.89, ADBE -1.8% to 304.44 (deceleration vs prior day's -5.4% breakdown, still above my 300 acceleration trigger). Meanwhile COST and GOOGL remain firm/at highs (950.98 and 335.84), confirming this is sector-wide risk-off rather than name-specific deterioration. Per my stated plan, ADBE further trim is only warranted if it breaks through 300 with continued volume - not there yet (low was 302.47), so holding the reduced position rather than trimming further. Cash buffer is healthy at ~18.8% of NAV from prior COST/ADBE trims, giving room to absorb this volatility without forced action. Not adding to any names into a broad down day without a clear reversal signal, and not panic-selling quality names (MSFT, META, AMZN, AVGO) on a one-day market-wide move. Will reconsider: trim ADBE further if it breaks decisively through 300 with volume; trim MSFT/META/AMZN if their declines extend past 10-12% from recent highs with no stabilization; add to any of these if a clear reversal/basing signal appears given cash on hand.

Continued broad tech softness on Jan 15, but no new decisive signals crossing my stated thresholds. MSFT closed 456.66 (-9.3% off Dec 31 high, marginal extension from Jan14's -8.7%), still short of my 10-12% trim trigger. META closed 620.80, actually up slightly from Jan14's 615.52 low - tentative stabilization, not a reversal signal yet. AMZN closed 238.18, also up from 236.65 - similar mild stabilization. AVGO ticked up to 343.02 from 339.89. ADBE closed 304.09, essentially flat vs 304.44, still holding above my 300 breakdown trigger with no renewed volume spike (4.8M vs the 7.2M breakdown day). COST remains firm and extending to new highs (956.75). GOOGL pulled back modestly to 332.78 from 335.84 highs but remains well above its base - normal consolidation. AAPL continues to grind in its 257-261 range, no decisive break either direction. Given cash buffer is already healthy (~18.8% of NAV), and today's action shows early signs of stabilization in the megacap decliners (META, AMZN both up slightly) rather than acceleration, there's no clear case for further defensive trims. Equally, no clean reversal/basing confirmation (e.g., a strong up day with volume) to justify redeploying cash yet. Holding all positions unchanged. Will reconsider: trim MSFT if it breaks below ~450 (would push past -11% off highs) or trims further deteriorate without stabilization; add to META/AMZN/ADBE if a strong reversal day with volume confirms the current tentative stabilization; trim ADBE further only on a decisive break through 300 with volume.

No new trading session data since Jan 16 close (market closed for MLK holiday Jan 19). Acting on the stabilization/breakdown thresholds set in prior journals using the latest available Jan 16 data: ADBE closed 296.12, decisively through my stated 300 breakdown trigger, on volume of 8.53M - higher than the original 7.2M breakdown-day volume on Jan 13, confirming acceleration rather than the flat/stabilizing pattern seen in MSFT/META/AMZN. This crosses my explicit rule from the Jan 14 journal to trim further on a decisive break through 300 with volume. Exiting the remaining ADBE position (4.98 units, ~$1,475) entirely rather than partial trim, since the position has now declined ~15.6% below average cost with no basing signal and deteriorating technicals (fresh multi-week low, expanding volume). Other positions unchanged: MSFT at 459.86 is still short of my -450 trim trigger (~-9.3% off highs, same as prior session, no further deterioration); META (620.25) and AMZN (239.12) showing continued stabilization near recent lows, not extending losses; GOOGL, COST, LIN, AAPL, AVGO all within normal ranges with no decisive breaks. Will reconsider redeploying the added cash buffer if a clear reversal/basing signal emerges in ADBE or other decliners, or continue trimming MSFT if it breaks below 450.

Jan 20 session showed a broad, market-wide risk-off decline rather than idiosyncratic breakdown: AAPL -3.5% to 246.70 (fresh low, huge volume 80M vs ~40-50M average - notable but no company-specific news available to me), AVGO -5.4% to 332.60, GOOGL -2.4% to 322.00, AMZN -3.4% to 231.00 (new low below prior 236.65 support), META -2.6% to 604.12 (breaking below its Jan14 low of 615.52, now ~12% off recent highs), MSFT -1.2% to 454.52 (still above my explicit 450 trim trigger by a small margin), COST and LIN holding up relatively well (964.26, 433.15) confirming this isn't a full capitulation but a broad tech/growth pullback. No individual name has crossed a pre-set actionable threshold: MSFT hasn't broken 450, and I already exited ADBE on its breakdown. AMZN and META are extending new lows which is a mild concern, but a single broad down day across nearly every major holding (defensive COST/LIN aside) reads as macro-driven de-risking rather than stock-specific deterioration, and panic-selling quality megacaps into such a day has not historically been rewarded per my own stated playbook. Cash buffer is already substantial (~22% of NAV) from prior ADBE exit, giving ample room to absorb further volatility without forced selling. Holding all positions unchanged today. Will reconsider: trim MSFT if it decisively breaks below 450; trim AMZN/META further if declines extend past 15% off highs without stabilization within the next few sessions; look to redeploy cash into any of these names on a clear reversal/basing day with strong volume, especially in COST/GOOGL/LIN which remain relatively firm.

Jan 21 session showed a key divergence from the prior broad-selloff pattern: MSFT closed 444.11, decisively breaking through my explicit 450 trim trigger (down from 454.52, on elevated volume 37.98M vs recent 23-34M range) - this confirms deteriorating momentum in MSFT specifically, not just macro noise. AVGO also extended its decline to 328.80 (new low in this window, down again from 332.60), continuing to make fresh lows while several peers bounced. In contrast, GOOGL (+2.0% to 328.38), META (+1.5% to 612.96), AAPL (+0.4% to 247.65), and COST (+1.9% to new high 982.86) all rebounded from Jan 20's lows on the same session - a mild reversal/stabilization signal in those names per my stated playbook. This divergence (MSFT/AVGO extending weakness while GOOGL/META/AAPL/COST/LIN stabilize or make new highs) suggests rotating some risk out of the laggards rather than treating this as uniform macro risk-off. Trimming 50% of MSFT (crossed my explicit threshold) and 50% of AVGO (persistent relative weakness, no bounce with peers) to raise cash further and reduce exposure to the names showing the most technical damage. Holding AAPL, GOOGL, AMZN, META, LIN, COST unchanged - these are either stabilizing (GOOGL, META, AAPL) or at highs (COST, LIN relatively firm). Will reconsider: redeploy cash into COST/GOOGL/LIN/META if the Jan21 bounce extends with continued volume confirmation over the next 1-2 sessions; re-enter MSFT/AVGO only on a clear basing pattern with volume, not immediately on further dips.

Jan 22 session confirmed a two-day bounce building in GOOGL and META off the Jan20 broad selloff low: GOOGL 322.00->328.38->330.54 (two consecutive up days, steady) and META 604.12->612.96->647.63 (accelerating, +5.6% on Jan22 with rising volume 21.4M vs 14.5M prior day - the strongest confirmation signal in the portfolio). AAPL also posted a second mild up day (246.70->247.65->248.35) but weaker magnitude. COST pulled back slightly from its Jan21 high (982.86->976.17) on lighter volume, so no new buy there despite still being well above its Jan20 low - staying pat. MSFT bounced off Jan21's 444.11 low to 451.14, but on lower volume than the breakdown day, so this reads as a single relief bounce rather than confirmed basing per my stated threshold (need a clearer multi-day basing pattern with volume before re-adding) - holding current trimmed MSFT position unchanged. AVGO continued to make a fresh low (325.49, down again from 328.80) with no bounce alongside peers - confirms persistent relative weakness, staying light there with no add. Deploying a modest slice of the ~31% cash buffer into GOOGL and META given the two-day confirmed reversal, while keeping AAPL, AMZN, LIN, COST, MSFT, AVGO positions unchanged and retaining a substantial cash cushion (~$10k) for further volatility. Will reconsider: add to COST/LIN if they resume making new highs with volume; re-enter MSFT/AVGO only on a multi-day basing pattern with confirming volume, not a single bounce day; trim GOOGL/META again if the bounce reverses and breaks back below Jan20 lows.

Jan 23 session delivered the confirmed multi-day basing pattern in MSFT I was waiting for: after bottoming at 444.11 (Jan21, breakdown volume 37.98M) and a tentative low-volume bounce to 451.14 (Jan22, 25.3M), MSFT surged to 465.95 (+3.3%) on Jan23 with volume of 38.0M - matching/exceeding the original breakdown volume. This is a genuine reversal confirmation (price + volume), not a single relief bounce, satisfying my previously stated re-entry threshold. Re-adding ~$3000 to MSFT using part of the cash buffer. AVGO continues to make fresh lows (320.05, down again from 325.49) with zero bounce alongside peers across this entire window - persistent relative weakness confirmed again, no add, keeping the small remaining position as-is rather than fighting the trend both ways. GOOGL pulled back mildly (330.54->327.93) on light volume after its two-day bounce - not a breakdown, just a pause, holding unchanged. META, LIN, COST all continue making new highs/strong closes (658.76, 451.57, 983.25) - holding these winners unchanged, no need to add at already-elevated multiples given the concentration already present. AAPL flat/steady around 248, holding. AMZN bounced to 239.16 with decent volume, holding unchanged. Retaining a still-meaningful cash cushion (~$7.4k) after this MSFT add for further opportunities or protection. Will reconsider: add further to MSFT only on continued follow-through with volume, trim if it reverses back below 450; re-enter AVGO only on an actual bounce day with volume (still hasn't happened); trim COST/LIN/META if they show a sharp reversal off these highs.

Jan 26 session: broad continuation of the recovery across the book. MSFT extended its confirmed basing breakout to 470.28 (from 465.95), well clear of the 450 trim trigger - holding, no further add needed given prior add already captured this move. META continues making fresh highs (672.36, up from 658.76) on solid volume - letting winners run, no new buy at these levels given concentration. LIN also at new highs (455.03). COST pulled back slightly intraday (993 high -> 977.67 close) but still near highs, not a breakdown - holding. GOOGL and AMZN both choppy/range-bound (GOOGL 322-335, AMZN 231-240), no clear signal either way - holding. AVGO bounced modestly to 324.85 from 320.05 but on lower volume than the prior down day (25M vs 30M) - not yet a confirmed reversal per my stated threshold, staying light with no add. AAPL stands out: broke out of its multi-day 246-258 consolidation range with a strong +3.3% day (251.48->255.41) on elevated volume (55.97M vs ~40M recent average) - this looks like genuine breakout confirmation, adding a modest $1500 tranche. Retaining remaining cash cushion (~$5.9k) for further opportunities/protection. Will reconsider: trim AAPL if it reverses back below 248; add further to AAPL on continued follow-through with volume; re-enter AVGO more meaningfully only on a stronger volume-confirmed bounce; trim COST/LIN/META winners only on a sharp reversal off highs.

Jan 27 session review: broad book still healthy. MSFT extended further to 480.58 (from 470.28) on steady volume - strong continuation, holding unchanged, no new add needed given large existing position. AAPL held gains at 258.27 after the breakout, consolidating near highs (259-262 range) - holding. GOOGL steady at 334.55, range-bound, no signal. META made a marginal new high (672.97) but on notably lighter volume (13.3M vs 16-22M prior sessions) - momentum cooling, holding but watching for reversal. LIN pulled back slightly (455.03->453.03) on low volume, just consolidation, holding. COST continued a mild pullback from its 993 high to 970.28 on light volume - not a breakdown, holding unchanged. AVGO now shows a genuine two-day bounce with confirming volume: 320.05->324.85->332.79, second consecutive up day with volume (25.5M) similar to the prior up day rather than fading - this finally meets my stated re-entry threshold after weeks of relative weakness. Adding a modest $800 tranche. AMZN broke out to a fresh local high (244.68, above its recent 231-240 range) on elevated volume (38.0M vs ~33-45M recent range, notably above the prior two sessions' ~32-33M) - looks like genuine breakout confirmation after weeks of chop, adding a modest $800 tranche. Keeping remaining cash cushion (~$4.3k) for further opportunities/protection given the account is already heavily invested (~89%). Will reconsider: add further to AVGO/AMZN on continued follow-through with volume, trim either if they reverse back below their recent range; trim META if it breaks below 660 on volume; trim COST/LIN only on a sharp reversal off highs.

Jan 28 session: broad mild pullback across the book after the recent run, nothing broken. MSFT still strong at 481.63 (new closing high territory), holding. AAPL pulled back to 256.44 from 258.27, still well above the 248 trim trigger, holding. GOOGL flat at 336.01. AMZN opened higher (246.37) but faded to close 243.01, down from 244.68 - normal digestion after Tuesday's breakout, not a reversal signal (still well above the 231-240 prior range), holding. META eased to 668.73 from 672.97 on light volume - still well above the 660 watch level, holding. LIN drifted to 451.50, mild consolidation, holding. COST continued its slow fade from the 993 high to 960.78, still not a sharp breakdown, holding. AVGO gave back some of its two-day bounce (339.99 high -> 333.24 close, basically flat vs prior close) - watching closely, would trim on a clear break back below 320 with volume. No new buy signal strong enough to deploy the remaining ~$4.3k cash cushion today; nothing crossed a reconsideration threshold that would justify a trim either. Holding entire book unchanged. Will reconsider: add to AVGO only on a fresh volume-confirmed bounce above 335; trim AAPL below 248; trim META below 660; trim AMZN below 231; trim COST/LIN only on sharp reversal off highs.

Major overnight events on Jan 29: MSFT gapped down hard from 481.63 close to open 439.99, closing at 433.50 on 128.9M volume (vs 25-37M typical range) - roughly a 10% one-day decline on 4x+ normal volume, clearly an earnings-driven repricing, not noise. This blows through my stated 450 trim trigger decisively. Rather than catch a falling knife on what looks like a fundamental reset, exiting the entire MSFT position now while it's still fresh - will reconsider re-entry only after the stock stabilizes and shows a real basing pattern with confirming volume, not on a single bounce day.

META moved the opposite direction: gapped up from 668.73 to open 737.43, closing 738.31 on 59.9M volume (vs 13-25M typical) - a ~10% single-day gain on very strong confirming volume, likely a strong earnings beat. Position has run up a lot already and is now a large concentration; trimming a small slice (3 units, ~15% of the position) to lock in some profit while keeping the bulk of the position to let the confirmed winner run. Will add back only on a clean pullback/retest of the breakout level with volume, or trim further if it gives back the gap on volume.

Everything else (AAPL, GOOGL, AMZN, LIN, COST, AVGO) traded in normal ranges with no threshold breaches - holding unchanged. Freed-up cash from the MSFT exit and META trim (~$7.7k on top of existing ~$4.3k) will sit as a buffer given the elevated single-stock volatility just witnessed in earnings season; will look to redeploy into confirmed setups in the current holdings or watch for new opportunities rather than force a new position today.

Post Jan-29 MSFT exit and META trim, cash cushion had built up to ~62k (62% of NAV) after the Feb 2 deposit landed - too defensive given the rest of the book (AAPL, GOOGL, AMZN, LIN, AVGO, COST) is trading in healthy uptrends with no threshold breaches. Redeploying roughly $33k of that cushion: modest adds to the six existing core positions that remain above their stated trim triggers (AAPL well above 248, GOOGL range-bound near highs, AMZN above 231 despite a mild pullback from 244.68, LIN steady near highs, AVGO holding its bounce above 320, COST still only a gradual fade from its 993 high, not a sharp break). Also initiating a new NVDA position ($8k) - it has been consolidating in a tight 178-194 range for two weeks without a breakdown, giving diversification exposure to AI/semis beyond AVGO without chasing an extended name. Skipped MSFT re-entry: it's still sliding (481->433->430) with no basing pattern yet per my prior thesis - need a real base with volume before considering it again. Skipped QCOM (steady downtrend) and MU (violent whipsaw, -9% intraday range on Jan 30 with elevated volume - too risky right now). META held unchanged - large position already trimmed once, still well above the 660 watch level at 716.5, letting it run. Keeping ~$29k cash buffer for opportunities/protection. Will reconsider: trim AAPL below 248, GOOGL on a clear break of the 320-330 range, AMZN below 231, META below 660, COST/LIN on sharp reversal off highs, AVGO below 320, NVDA on a break below 178 support; add to MSFT only after a confirmed multi-day base with volume.

Feb 3 review: no threshold breaches across the book. AAPL closed at a fresh high (270.01, up from 246-260 range) on solid volume - strong continuation, well above the 248 trim trigger, no action needed since already sized appropriately after yesterday's add. GOOGL also pushed to a new high (343.69) continuing its range-bound-to-breakout move, no trim trigger hit. AMZN steady at 242.96, above 231 support. LIN at 460.16, calm uptrend. AVGO 331.11, holding above the 320 watch level after a mild pullback from 336 intraday. COST rebounded sharply to 968.36 from the 940 dip, no breakdown concern. NVDA still consolidating in the 178-194 range (185.61 close), no breakout or breakdown yet - holding the new position from yesterday without adding until it resolves the range. META continues to fade off its earnings spike (706.41, down from 738 peak) but remains far above the 660 watch level - normal digestion of a huge gap, no action. MSFT still weak (423.37, sliding further) with no basing pattern - continuing to skip re-entry per prior thesis. QCOM and MU both remain in downtrend/high-volatility territory - passing again. Choosing to hold the entire book unchanged today rather than chase AAPL/GOOGL's new highs or force a trade; ~29% cash buffer remains appropriate for flexibility. Will reconsider: trim AAPL below 248, GOOGL on a clear break of 320-330, AMZN below 231, META below 660, COST/LIN on a sharp reversal off highs, AVGO below 320, NVDA on a break below 178; add to MSFT only after a confirmed multi-day base with volume; consider NVDA add only on a confirmed breakout above 194.

Feb 4 review: increased volatility in AVGO and NVDA but no confirmed close-based threshold breach yet. AVGO printed a wide range on 2/3 (high 338.9, low 308.65) on elevated volume (36.9M vs ~25M typical) before closing back at 320.33 - right at my 320 watch level. The intraday wick well below 320 is a warning sign but the close held the line, so treating this as heightened risk to monitor rather than a confirmed breakdown; not adding, not trimming yet. NVDA similarly wicked down to 176.23 intraday (piercing my 178 support) on volume of 204M (above its recent 140-180M range) but closed at 180.34, still above support on a closing basis. Same treatment: watch closely, no action today - a close below 178 would trigger an exit.
